events.text: Rumi on Patience: Waiting, Trust and the Water of Life
events.sub: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
events.fa: مولانا و صبر

events.text: Patience is one of the oldest words in the Sufi path.
For Rumi it is not a grey, dutiful waiting. It is a quiet trust that something is ripening out of sight.
Here are eight passages from his Masnavi and his Divan-e Shams about how to wait.

events.fa: صبر و خاموشی جذوب رحمتست
events.en: Patience and silence draw mercy in;

events.fa: وین نشان جستن نشان علتست
events.en: and this demanding of signs is itself a sign of sickness.

events.fa: انصتوا بپذیر تا بر جان تو
events.en: Accept the command "Be silent," so that upon your soul

events.fa: آید از جانان جزای انصتوا
events.en: the reward of that silence may come from the Beloved.

events.text: In this part of the Masnavi, people keep asking the prophets for miracles and proofs.
Rumi answers that patience and silence are what actually draw mercy toward us.
"Be silent" is a phrase from the Quran: when the Word is recited, listen.
When we stop demanding signs and simply listen, something can finally reach us.
Patience, here, begins as a kind of listening.

fa: صبر و خاموشی جذوب رحمتست
وین نشان جستن نشان علتست
انصتوا بپذیر تا بر جان تو
آید از جانان جزای انصتوا

events.fa: تا نگویی در زمستان باغ را مستی نماند
events.en: Do not say that in winter the garden has lost its joy;

events.fa: مدتی پنهان شدست از دیده مکار مست
events.en: for a while, the drunken one has hidden from the cunning eye.

events.fa: بیخهای آن درختان می نهانی میخورند
events.en: The roots of those trees are drinking wine in secret.

events.fa: روزکی دو صبر میکن تا شود بیدار مست
events.en: Be patient a day or two, until the drunken one awakes.

events.text: This ghazal is full of drunkenness, Rumi's image for joy and life in God.
In winter the garden looks dead. Nothing seems to be happening.
But Rumi says the roots are drinking in secret, under the ground.
Many of our hardest seasons are like that: the work is happening where we cannot see it.
Wait a little. Spring is only asleep.

fa: تا نگویی در زمستان باغ را مستی نماند
مدتی پنهان شدست از دیده مکار مست
بیخهای آن درختان می نهانی میخورند
روزکی دو صبر میکن تا شود بیدار مست

events.fa: پنبه ز گوش دور کن بانگ نجات میرسد
events.en: Take the cotton from your ears: the call of rescue is coming.

events.fa: آب سیاه درمرو کآب حیات میرسد
events.en: Do not walk into the black water, for the water of life is coming.

events.fa: در ظلمات ابتلا صبر کن و مکن ابا
events.en: In the darkness of trial, be patient, and do not refuse;

events.fa: کآب حیات خضر را در ظلمات میرسد
events.en: for Khidr found the water of life in the darkness.

events.text: In Persian legend, Khidr is the green wanderer who found the spring of eternal life.
And he found it in the Land of Darkness, a place no one wanted to enter.
Rumi takes that story and hands it to anyone who is suffering.
Do not run from the dark, he says. Do not give up in it.
The water of life is found exactly there.

fa: پنبه ز گوش دور کن بانگ نجات میرسد
آب سیاه درمرو کآب حیات میرسد
در ظلمات ابتلا صبر کن و مکن ابا
کآب حیات خضر را در ظلمات میرسد

events.fa: بی صبر بود و بیحیل خود را بکشت او از عجل
events.en: It had no patience and no skill; it killed itself in haste.

events.fa: گر صبر کردی یک زمان رستی از او آن بدلقا
events.en: Had it been patient for one moment, that ugly creature would have left it alone.

events.fa: بر خارپشت هر بلا خود را مزن تو هم هلا
events.en: Beware: do not throw yourself, too, against the hedgehog of every trouble.

events.fa: ساکن نشین وین ورد خوان «جاء القضا ضاق الفضا»
events.en: Sit still, and repeat this: "When fate arrives, the wide world grows narrow."

events.text: Just before these lines, Rumi tells of a foolish snake that meets a hedgehog.
It strikes again and again at the thorns, until it is pierced all over by its own attacks.
If it had only been still for a moment, the hedgehog would have gone on its way.
How often do we wound ourselves by fighting a trouble that would have passed?
Rumi's advice is simple: sit still, and let the moment pass.

fa: بی صبر بود و بیحیل خود را بکشت او از عجل
گر صبر کردی یک زمان رستی از او آن بدلقا
بر خارپشت هر بلا خود را مزن تو هم هلا
ساکن نشین وین ورد خوان «جاء القضا ضاق الفضا»

events.fa: فرمود رب العالمین با صابرانم همنشین
events.en: The Lord of the worlds has said: I sit with those who are patient.

events.fa: ای همنشین صابران «افرغ علینا صبرنا»
events.en: O Companion of the patient, "pour out patience upon us."

events.text: Both halves of this line echo the Quran.
God is with the patient, it says; and the prayer: our Lord, pour patience upon us.
Notice what Rumi does. He does not tell us to produce patience by force.
He asks for it, the way a dry field asks for rain.
Patience, for him, is a gift we can pray for, and a companionship we are never alone in.

fa: فرمود رب العالمین با صابرانم همنشین
ای همنشین صابران «افرغ علینا صبرنا»

events.fa: عقل اگر قاضیست کو خط و منشور او
events.en: If reason is a judge, where is its writ, its decree?

events.fa: دیدن پایان کار صبر و وقار و وفاست
events.en: To see how things end, that takes patience, dignity and faithfulness.

events.text: The clever mind likes to judge quickly. It wants a verdict today.
Rumi asks: by what authority?
Only someone who waits, calmly and faithfully, gets to see how the story really ends.
Much of what looked like failure turns out, later, to be the turning of the road.
Patience is the only seat from which the whole story can be seen.

fa: عقل اگر قاضیست کو خط و منشور او
دیدن پایان کار صبر و وقار و وفاست

events.fa: کسی کو یار صبر آمد سوار ماه و ابر آمد
events.en: Whoever takes patience as a friend comes riding on the moon and the clouds.

events.fa: مکن باور که ابر تر گدای ناودان باشد
events.en: Do not believe that the rain-heavy cloud is a beggar at the gutter.

events.text: Here patience is not weakness. It is a kind of royalty.
The one who befriends it rides on the moon and the clouds.
And the cloud full of rain does not beg from the gutter. The gutter lives from the cloud.
The patient heart is like that cloud: full, and not in need of crumbs.
Waiting, done well, is a form of strength.

fa: کسی کو یار صبر آمد سوار ماه و ابر آمد
مکن باور که ابر تر گدای ناودان باشد

events.fa: به جان پاک تو ای معدن سخا و وفا
events.en: By your pure soul, O mine of generosity and faithfulness,

events.fa: که صبر نیست مرا بیتو ای عزیز بیا
events.en: I have no patience without you. Beloved, come.

events.fa: چه جای صبر که گر کوه قاف بود این صبر
events.en: What room is there for patience? Even if this patience were Mount Qaf,

events.fa: ز آفتاب جدایی چو برف گشت فنا
events.en: under the sun of separation it melted away like snow.

events.text: And to end, Rumi turns everything upside down.
Mount Qaf is the mountain at the edge of the world in Persian legend, the biggest thing imaginable.
Even a patience that large melts like snow in the heat of separation.
This is the honest side of patience: sometimes love simply cannot wait, and says so.
Rumi lets us be patient, and lets us cry out "come". Both are part of the path.

fa: به جان پاک تو ای معدن سخا و وفا
که صبر نیست مرا بیتو ای عزیز بیا
چه جای صبر که گر کوه قاف بود این صبر
ز آفتاب جدایی چو برف گشت فنا

events.text: Thank you for waiting with these verses.
Every week we share real passages of Rumi, translated honestly from the Persian.
If they spoke to you, subscribe to The Guest House.
